theme: Type 2 immunity: Th2, IL-4/IL-13/IL-33 and mast cells
story: The centre is Th2 differentiation of naive CD4+ T cells and the production and signalling of the Th2 cytokines IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13, with paired positive and negative regulation terms showing how this programme is dialled up and down. IL-33 signalling acts as an upstream alarmin that drives Th2 and mast-cell responses, while mast cell activation, FcERI-mediated NF-kB activation and isotype switching to IgE form the effector arm in which IgE-armed mast cells release cytokines. Together the cluster describes the type 2 immune response used against helminths (response to nematode) and underlying allergy.

theme: Neural inhibition and sensorimotor and social behaviour
story: This cluster centres on organism-level behaviours read out in animal models: exploration, psychomotor activity, grooming, swimming, social interaction, visual behaviour, touch perception and prepulse inhibition. The molecular members tie these to inhibitory neurotransmission: glycine transporter SLC6A5 defects cause hyperekplexia (exaggerated startle), MECP2 regulates GABA-signalling genes, and negative regulation of nerve impulse transmission dampens excitability, with amygdala development supplying the circuitry for emotional and social behaviour. As a whole it links inhibitory signalling balance to sensorimotor gating and behaviour, the phenotype space of neurodevelopmental disorders like Rett syndrome.

theme: Neurotrophin Trk receptor signalling to MAPK cascades
story: The core is NTF3 activating its receptor NTRK3, which signals through three canonical adaptor routes: RAS, PI3K and PLCG1. Shared Trk downstream machinery (FRS2- and ARMS-mediated activation, RIT/RIN signalling to p38, signalling to ERK5, Ras positive regulation) and ligand-independent TRKA activation broaden it to the Trk family generally, with MAP2K mutants representing oncogenic dysregulation of the same MAPK route. The pathway terminates in CREB phosphorylation, so the cluster as a whole describes how neurotrophin receptors convert growth-factor binding into MAPK-driven transcription for neuronal survival and differentiation.

theme: Early neural plate patterning and neural crest specification
story: The centre is formation and patterning of the early neural plate: anterior and posterior neural plate formation, specification of the neural plate border, and dorsal/ventral axis determination. Hindbrain segmentation (rhombomere development, anterior HOX gene activation, midbrain-hindbrain boundary and anatomical boundary formation) supplies anteroposterior regional identity, while the TFAP2 (AP-2) transcription factor terms describe the regulator that specifies the neural plate border and drives neural crest fate commitment. Together the cluster describes how the embryonic ectoderm is subdivided along both axes into neural tube regions and the neural crest.

theme: cAMP-PKA second messenger signalling to CREB
story: The centre is the cAMP route: adenylate cyclase activation (including calcium/calmodulin-stimulated ADCY1/ADCY8 and forskolin response) produces cAMP, which activates protein kinase A and leads to CREB1 phosphorylation and CREB-dependent transcription. The termination arm, cAMP catabolism by calmodulin-activated PDE1 and negative regulation of cAMP/PKA signalling, sets the duration and amplitude of the signal, while GPCR inputs such as HTR6 and CaMKII restraint tune it. The cluster as a whole describes how a second messenger is generated, read out and switched off, notably in neuronal plasticity.

theme: Glutamate-centred nitrogen and amino acid metabolism, urea cycle
story: Glutamate, glutamine and 2-oxoglutarate form the hub, interconverting nitrogen-carrying amino acids by transamination and deamination. Connected around it are the glutamate-family amino acids (proline synthesis and catabolism, ornithine, arginine catabolism, citrulline), the aspartate family, and GABA degradation that feeds back to glutamate and succinate. The urea-cycle and ammonia terms (ammonium homeostasis, cellular response to ammonium, urea-cycle enzyme regulation, SLC25A15 ornithine transporter defects causing HHH syndrome) show the cluster's purpose: managing nitrogen flux and safely disposing of ammonia.

theme: Synapse assembly by trans-synaptic adhesion molecules
story: The centre is trans-synaptic adhesion: neurexins and neuroligins, synaptic adhesion-like molecules (SALMs) and receptor-type tyrosine phosphatases bridge pre- and postsynaptic membranes. These contacts drive presynaptic assembly (presynaptic membrane, terminal buttons, synaptic vesicle clustering) and postsynaptic assembly (PSD-95 and NMDA receptor clustering, postsynaptic membrane assembly). The positive and negative regulation of excitatory postsynaptic potentials is the functional outcome, so the cluster describes how adhesion organizes and tunes excitatory synapses.

theme: Cellular energy carriers: adenine nucleotides, NAD(P), phosphocreatine
story: The centre is maintenance of the cell's energy and redox cofactor pools: interconversion of nucleotide di- and triphosphates, nucleoside monophosphate phosphorylation, ADP and GTP synthesis, and mitochondrial ATP/ADP exchange. The creatine/phosphocreatine system acts as an energy buffer, and the nicotinate metabolism, pyridine nucleotide salvage, NADP+ synthesis, NAD+ catabolism and NAD transport terms cover the parallel redox-cofactor supply. Together they describe the small-molecule bookkeeping that keeps ATP and NAD(P) available for metabolism.

The centre is the NLRP1 and NLRP3 inflammasomes, which activate caspase-1 to process the precursors of IL-1 and IL-18 (cytokine precursor processing, IL-1 processing). Downstream, IL-18 production and signalling and IL-1 alpha and CXCL1 production carry the inflammatory output, while purinergic (ATP-P2X7) signalling in leishmaniasis is a trigger of NLRP3 activation, and protein homotrimerization reflects receptor/channel assembly in the pathway. The cluster as a whole describes how innate danger sensing is converted into release of IL-1 family cytokines.

theme: NGF/Trk signalling through MAPK cascades to transcription
story: The centre is neurotrophin (NGF/TrkA) receptor signalling, including ligand-independent TRKA activation and the FRS2- and ARMS-mediated adaptor routes. These feed several MAPK cascades: classic RAS-ERK, ERK5, p38 and the atypical MAPK6/MAPK4 route, which converge on nuclear targets through CREB phosphorylation and NGF-stimulated transcription. The cluster as a whole describes how growth-factor receptor activation is relayed via MAPK modules into gene expression for neuronal survival and differentiation.
